walkthroughs.body_html: (.) = micropause. (2.0) = two-second pause. [ = overlap. CAPS = stressed.

'You're going?' (rising) = checking.

'You're going.' (falling) = statement.

Same words, different speech act.

'It's quite hot, ISN'T IT?' invites agreement and builds rapport.

Janet Holmes showed tag questions often serve a SOCIAL — not informational — purpose.

mcqs.q: Why do text types have predictable features?
options: Text types are arbitrary and have no patterns.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
Text types have fixed features just because tradition says so.
Conventions develop because they serve communicative purpose — a recipe needs imperatives because it instructs; a news report needs the inverted pyramid because of how readers scan.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between voiced and voiceless sounds?
options: A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
Voiced sounds are produced with vocal-fold vibration (/b/, /d/, /g/, /z/); voiceless sounds without it (/p/, /t/, /k/, /s/). You can feel the difference by putting a hand on your throat.
Voiced sounds are loud and voiceless sounds are whispered.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
